description: Migration adds documents.audience (text, not null, check constraint on requester/shared_it/organization_private)
Migration adds document_folders.audience with the same constraint
Backfill: is_client_visible = true becomes requester, everything else organization_private, on both tables
Backfill: a document created by a user holding a seat assignment becomes shared_it when it was not client-visible
is_client_visible on documents and document_folders becomes derived from audience = 'requester' (stored generated column, or the constrained fallback if Citus refuses it)
Migration runs on a distributed Citus schema and on a plain Postgres CE schema
IDocument and the folder type carry audience; is_client_visible stays as a read-only derived field
The comment audience predicate (TypeScript and SQL forms) becomes a content-audience predicate that takes an audience expression, with comments as one caller
Documents call the content-audience predicate with their audience column, in the record check and in the SQL read scope
Creation default by author: MSP staff organization_private, seat technician shared_it, portal user requester
An explicit audience at creation is accepted only from the author's allowed set; a seat technician cannot choose organization_private and a portal user can only choose requester
Folder inheritance: an upload takes the folder's audience when wider than the author's default and is never narrower than the author's floor

Every document writer sets audience instead of is_client_visible: createDocumentFromCommittedFile, addDocument, the resumable upload route, inline image uploads, comment attachment drafts, email and telephony ingestion, asset custody, invoice and billing document writers, API services
Default entity folders (document_default_folders) seed folder audience
Record guard shared_audience (JS and SQL facets) in the record-guard registry
Record guard attached_parents_in_scope (JS and SQL facets): every attached ticket is in the seat's client and boards, every attached project task belongs to a shared project
Document authorization records carry audience and the attached project tasks with their project ids
Document SQL adapter maps the audience column and the attached-project-task facet
Seat policy for document read and create becomes own_client, shared_audience, attached_parents_in_scope; client_visible_or_in_scope_ticket and attached_tickets_in_scope are removed
Create-time authorization (isDocumentAssociationCreateAllowed) evaluates the candidate record with the audience the document will be stored with
Portal denial reads audience = 'requester'; portal behaviour is unchanged
Comment-attachment documents keep audience requester and stay governed by the comment's audience through the existing attachment gate
setDocumentAudience action: MSP staff with document:update set any audience on a document they can read; seat technicians and portal users are refused
Folder audience setters (by id and by path) replace the boolean folder visibility toggles; the boolean actions remain as thin callers
shared_it is refused by every writer in a tenant the co-managed capability does not serve, by edition and capability, not by flag
REST and MCP document schemas expose audience on read and accept it on write; is_client_visible-only writes map to requester or the author's default; conflicting values are rejected
A tenant with no seat arrangement keeps today's client-visibility control unchanged (component, labels, placement); it writes organization_private and requester
Three-state audience control for a tenant with at least one seat arrangement, on the document row, document drawer, upload dialog and folder visibility control, using the standard select
The control's mode is decided by the existence of a seat arrangement row for the tenant, not by edition, licence or the co-managed capability alone
Seat technician upload dialog offers Shared with client IT (default) and Client-visible
Document lists keep today's client-visible indicator unchanged for a tenant with no seat arrangement and show an audience badge in its place for a tenant with one
Locale strings for the three audience labels and their hints
